attacks.claim: Auto-download when the local slot is 'older' is decided from timestamps, and the 1.3 build ignores the sidecar. A 1.3 session that changes the local save without updating sidecar.last-modified, or a clock-skewed PC, can make the cloud copy look newer and silently replace local progress with no prompt. That breaks the stated rule that nothing is overwritten without the player's choice.
attacks.evidence: On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older. ... Nothing is overwritten without that choice.

attacks.claim: Version retention is count-based, not time-based. Five server versions per slot can be pushed out within minutes if autosave is frequent, and a valid-schema but semantically bad 1.4 write (which the checksum and schema checks would accept) would evict the last good copy. The artifact never states autosave frequency or a time-based floor for retention.
attacks.evidence: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally in saves/backup/

attacks.claim: The rollback claim is only partly tested. QA covers loading a 1.4 save in 1.3, but not a 1.3 session that saves back over a 1.4 file. A 1.3 write-back can drop the unknown modifier keys and leave sidecar.meta stale, so the next 1.4 launch sees a changed save with stale metadata.
attacks.evidence: Downgrade to 1.3 ... Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored

attacks.claim: No test exercises the production Epic path. The Epic build was run on the dev sandbox, and the Epic beta used sandbox testers, yet Epic linking validates EOS tokens against production in the shipping design. Epic validation and scope behaviour in production is unverified.
attacks.evidence: Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox pointed at the production Cross-Save backend ... Epic sandbox testers (150)

attacks.claim: The rollback plan says 1.3 is restored on both stores and that 1.4 saves load in 1.3 (tested above). The only downgrade test was on the Steam beta branch, so the Epic rollback path and its save compatibility are untested.
attacks.evidence: Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`) ... If the patch itself must be reverted, 1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores

attacks.claim: Age gating only exists for Epic cabined accounts. Steam accounts of minors can link, and their Steam IDs and save data are stored, with no described age check or parental consent path. That is a likely minors-consent gap under EU and COPPA-style rules.
attacks.evidence: Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered and the screen explains why.

attacks.claim: Unlink-and-delete is irreversible after 24 h and destroys all server copies, but the artifact does not say what authorizes it. It does not state whether it needs both store sessions, a fresh re-auth, or a confirmation step. On a shared PC or with a stolen short-lived token, a player's cloud saves could be destroyed.
attacks.evidence: Settings > Cross-Save > "Unlink and delete cloud saves" removes the link and all server copies within 24 h

attacks.claim: Quotas are per player, with no per-IP or global cap and no account-creation control. Farmed linked accounts can each drive 60 uploads/hour of up to 2 MB. The hard budget stop then flips the kill switch for all legitimate players, so a cheap abuse vector becomes a platform-wide outage of Cross-Save.
attacks.evidence: 60 uploads per hour per player ... hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically

attacks.claim: The storage forecast does not reconcile with the stated limits. At 60% of 182k players, 10 slots and 5 versions of 420 KB, the storage is about 2.3 TB, not 140 GB. The hard budget cap bounds the damage, but the forecast is unreliable.
attacks.evidence: ~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month

attacks.claim: The load test is 30k concurrent launches over 10 min, but the artifact gives no patch-day peak estimate to compare it with. Failure is graceful (local play continues), so this is not blocking.
attacks.evidence: Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors

attacks.claim: Deletion covers live server copies, but the artifact does not say how backups, replicas or logs holding Steam/Epic IDs and save blobs are purged after the 24 h window.
attacks.evidence: removes the link and all server copies within 24 h

attacks.claim: Billing alerts and the budget stop depend on billing data that typically lags. The $600 hard stop can overshoot, and the artifact does not mention this lag.
attacks.evidence: Cloud billing alert at $250/month and hard project budget stop at $600/month

attacks.claim: The public patch note says local saves 'stay where they are', but auto-download and the conflict flow can replace a local save's content. The copy overstates how stable local saves are.
attacks.evidence: Your saves on this PC stay where they are.

attacks.claim: Linking depends on Steam and Epic identity services and EOS token validation. This is an acceptable store dependency, but the exit cost is not described.
attacks.evidence: Epic Account Services scopes requested: basic profile id only

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy found; controller, keyboard, 200% scale, narration and Steam Deck are covered in QA.
attacks.evidence: Controller-only, keyboard-only and 200% UI scale on Cross-Save screens; screen narration for the conflict prompt | Pass

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy found; the offline path does not block the player and the conflict prompt is a single choice.
attacks.evidence: The game never blocks on the network

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy found; the feature is opt-in and the rollout includes a beta.
attacks.evidence: Cross-Save available to everyone who turns it on.

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-worthy found; the sidecar and modifier keys are isolated from the v3 format.
attacks.evidence: Save files are unchanged: same v3 format as 1.3.

attacks.claim: Monitoring has no alert on schema or checksum rejection rate, which would be an early signal of a bad 1.4 write.
attacks.evidence: Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate.
